steps: Algorithmic bias occurs when an AI system produces unfair or prejudiced results for certain people or groups.
It can arise from biased or incomplete training data, errors in data collection, or the way an algorithm is designed.
For example, a hiring system trained on biased past hiring records may unfairly favour some applicants over others.
Biased results can lead to discrimination and unequal treatment.
AI systems should be tested with diverse data and checked regularly for fairness.
items.finalAnswer: Algorithmic bias is unfair or prejudiced results produced by an AI system, often because of biased data or design.

steps: Ethical considerations guide the responsible development and use of AI and IoT.
Privacy must be protected by collecting only necessary data and keeping personal information secure.
AI systems should be fair and should not discriminate against individuals or groups.
People should be informed when AI or connected devices collect or use their data.
AI decisions should be transparent and accountable, especially when they affect people’s lives.
Security measures are important to protect IoT devices and their data from unauthorised access.
Responsible use helps build trust and reduces harm to individuals and society.
items.finalAnswer: Ethical considerations help ensure that AI and IoT are fair, secure, privacy-respecting, transparent, and used responsibly.

steps: AI can support personalised learning by adapting lessons and practice questions to a student's progress and needs.
For example, an adaptive learning application can provide easier or more challenging questions based on a student's answers.
AI tutoring systems can give students immediate feedback and guidance while they practise.
AI can help teachers assess work, identify learning gaps, and monitor student progress.
For example, an automated assessment tool can mark objective questions and show which topics need further teaching.
Educational chatbots can answer common questions and provide learning support when a teacher is not available.
AI can assist students with disabilities through tools such as speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and translation.
These applications can make learning more accessible and engaging and can help teachers use their time more effectively.
AI should be used responsibly, with attention to student privacy, fairness, and the continuing role of teachers.
items.finalAnswer: AI can personalise learning, provide tutoring and feedback, assist assessment, and improve accessibility, while supporting rather than replacing teachers.

steps: An explainable (whitebox) AI model has a decision-making process that can be understood and interpreted by people.
Its input, rules, or reasoning can be examined to help explain how it reached a result.
A simple decision tree is an example of a model whose decisions can usually be followed step by step.
An unexplainable (blackbox) AI model produces results through complex processes that are difficult for people to interpret.
In a blackbox model, it may be difficult to explain exactly why a particular result was produced.
Many complex machine-learning models, such as deep neural networks, can function as blackbox models.
Whitebox models are generally easier to explain and audit, while blackbox models may be difficult to interpret even when they produce useful results.
items.finalAnswer: Whitebox AI has decisions people can understand, whereas blackbox AI makes decisions through processes that are difficult to interpret.

steps: An IoT system consists of physical devices, sensors or actuators, a network connection, data processing, and a user interface or application.
Sensors collect information from the environment, such as temperature, movement, or location.
Actuators can carry out actions, such as switching a device on or off, in response to a command or processed data.
The network connection transfers data between the devices and other parts of the system, often through the internet.
A processing system, such as a computer, server, or cloud platform, stores and analyses the collected data.
A user interface or application lets users view information and control connected devices.
Together, these components collect data, communicate it, process it, and provide information or actions for an IoT application.
For example, a smart thermostat senses room temperature, sends data for processing, and can adjust heating based on the settings.
items.finalAnswer: IoT devices sense or act, communicate through a network, have their data processed, and provide information or control through an application.

steps: IoT can connect vehicles, roads, traffic signals, and transport control systems to exchange information.
GPS-enabled tracking can show the location of buses, taxis, delivery vehicles, or other transport in real time.
Connected traffic signals and road sensors can monitor traffic flow and help manage congestion.
Sensors in vehicles can monitor their condition and alert operators when maintenance is needed.
Public transport applications can provide passengers with live vehicle locations and estimated arrival times.
Fleet operators can use IoT data to plan routes, monitor vehicles, and improve the use of fuel and time.
Connected vehicle and road systems can provide warnings about hazards or changing road conditions.
These applications can make transportation more informed and efficient, but they require secure handling of location and travel data.
items.finalAnswer: IoT supports transportation through vehicle tracking, traffic management, vehicle monitoring, passenger updates, and fleet and route management.

steps: IoT devices may continuously collect personal information, such as location, daily routines, health readings, or activity in a home.
Users may not always know what data is being collected, how long it is stored, or who can access it.
Data may be shared with service providers or other organisations without users fully understanding or controlling the sharing.
Weak passwords, insecure devices, or unprotected networks can allow unauthorised access to devices and personal data.
A security breach may expose sensitive information or allow an attacker to control a connected device.
Combining data from several devices can reveal detailed information about a person's habits and behaviour.
Privacy risks can be reduced by limiting data collection, obtaining informed consent, securing devices and networks, and controlling access to data.
items.finalAnswer: IoT privacy concerns include excessive or unclear data collection, sharing without informed consent, tracking, and unauthorised access to personal information.

steps: AI and IoT can automate routine tasks and help workers make decisions using data.
Automation may reduce the need for some tasks or change the skills required in certain jobs.
At the same time, new work can be created in areas such as developing, maintaining, securing, and managing AI and IoT systems.
In workplaces, connected devices can monitor equipment, support remote work, and improve the organisation of tasks.
These technologies can increase productivity and assist workers, but they may also require workers to learn new skills.
Employers and educators can help workers adapt through training and opportunities to reskill.
The overall effect depends on how the technologies are adopted and how workers and organisations respond to the changes.
items.finalAnswer: AI and IoT can automate and transform jobs, create new technology-related work, and improve workplaces, while increasing the need for training and new skills.
